title: Arrow Function Implicit Return
code:
const double = n => n * 2;
console.log(double(5));

title: Arrow Function With Object Literal
code: const makeUser = name => { name: name };

bugs.explanation: Without parentheses, the `{}` after `=>` is parsed as a function body, not an object literal. `{ name: name }` inside a function body is a label followed by an expression statement — the function returns `undefined`. Wrap the object in parentheses: `=> ({ name: name })`.

flat() for Nested Arrays
code:
const nested = [1, [2, [3, 4]]];
console.log(nested.flat());

bugs.explanation: `flat()` with no argument only flattens one level deep. `[1, [2, [3, 4]]]` becomes `[1, 2, [3, 4]]` — the inner array is still nested. Use `flat(Infinity)` to fully flatten nested arrays of any depth.

title: forEach Returns Undefined

bugs.explanation: `forEach` always returns `undefined` — it is for side effects only. To produce a new array of transformed values, use `map` which returns the transformed array.

title: Array.indexOf Returns -1 When Missing

bugs.explanation: `indexOf` returns `-1` when the item is not found. `-1` is truthy, so `if (arr.indexOf('d'))` is `true` even when `'d'` is absent. Additionally, if the item is at index `0`, `indexOf` returns `0` which is falsy. Always compare explicitly: `=== -1` for not found, or use `arr.includes('d')`.

title: Rest Parameters Must Be Last

bugs.explanation: Rest parameters (`...messages`) must be the last parameter in a function signature — they collect all remaining arguments. Having a parameter after `...messages` is a `SyntaxError`. Reorder so rest comes last.

Missing Return in Arrow Function Body

bugs.explanation: When an arrow function uses curly braces `{}`, the body requires an explicit `return` statement. Without it, the function returns `undefined`. Either add `return n * 3;` or use the shorthand `n => n * 3` without braces.
